hero.title: Understand what every move says
hero.subtitle: Learn the language of chess in short, visual lessons. No prior knowledge and no walls of text.

notation.title: Read a game without translating it
notation.intro: Chess notation is a compact record of what happened. Piece letters are always in English, while pawns use no letter at all.
notation.piecesHelp: The first capital letter tells you which piece moved.
notation.pawnRule: A pawn move starts directly with its destination square: e4 means a pawn moved to e4.
notation.examplesHelp: Tap an example and see how each symbol changes the meaning.

examples.e4: A pawn moves to e4. Pawns do not write a letter.
examples.Bxf7+: The bishop (B) captures (x) on f7 and gives check (+).
examples.O-O: The king castles on the kingside.
examples.Rae1: The rook (R) from the a-file moves to e1. The “a” distinguishes it from the other rook.
examples.e8=Q#: A pawn reaches e8, promotes to a queen (=Q) and gives checkmate (#).

movement.title: See the board before memorising rules
movement.intro: Choose a piece. The board highlights every square it could reach from d4 on an otherwise empty board.

pieces.K: One square in any direction. It may never move onto a square attacked by the opponent.
pieces.Q: Any number of squares along ranks, files or diagonals. It cannot jump over pieces.
pieces.R: Any number of squares horizontally or vertically. It cannot jump over pieces.
pieces.B: Any number of squares diagonally. A bishop stays on the same square colour for the whole game.
pieces.N: In an L: two squares in one direction and one sideways. It is the only piece that can jump over others.
pieces.P: One square forward, but it captures one square diagonally. From its starting square it may advance two.

practice.title: Make the move on the board
practice.intro: Select the starting square and then the destination. If you miss, the Academy tells you why and lets you try again.
practice.incorrect: That move is not the one

knight.title: Find the knight jump
knight.prompt: Move the knight from f3 to e5.
knight.correct: Ne5 is legal: the knight moves two squares in one direction and one to the side.
knight.wrong: Start with the knight on f3 and land on e5. A knight never moves in a straight line; it jumps in an L.

rook.title: Use the open file
rook.prompt: Capture the rook on a8 with your rook from a1.
rook.correct: Rxa8+ uses the clear a-file, captures the rook and checks the king on g8.
rook.wrong: The rook must start on a1 and travel straight up the clear a-file to a8. Rooks do not move diagonally.

bishop.title: Give check on the diagonal
bishop.prompt: Move the bishop from c4 to b5 and check the king.
bishop.correct: Bb5+ keeps the bishop on its diagonal and points directly at the king on e8.
bishop.wrong: The bishop must go from c4 to b5. Bishops only move diagonally, and that square opens the checking line to e8.

classifications.title: Why a move gets each label
classifications.intro: NexoChess compares your move with the position and the engine alternatives. Tap any label for its plain-language meaning.
classifications.engineNote: The same move can receive a different label in another position: context, alternatives and the change in winning chances all matter.

descriptions.brilliant: A very strong, difficult move that deliberately leaves material exposed or sacrifices it for a sound idea.
descriptions.critical: A great move in a demanding position where the other serious alternatives are substantially worse.
descriptions.best: The engine's top move, verified without a meaningful loss in winning chances.
descriptions.excellent: Very close to the best choice. It preserves almost all of the position's value.
descriptions.okay: A sound move that keeps the game on track, although a more precise option existed.
descriptions.inaccuracy: A small slip. The position becomes somewhat worse, but the game is far from lost because of it.
descriptions.mistake: A significant error that clearly reduces your winning or drawing chances.
descriptions.miss: The opponent gave you an important opportunity and this move failed to take advantage of it.
descriptions.blunder: A major error that causes a large swing, such as losing material, an advantage or the game.
descriptions.forced: There was only one legal move, so there was no real decision to make.
descriptions.theory: A recognised opening move that remains inside known opening theory.
descriptions.risky: A legacy label for a dubious or unnecessarily dangerous idea. It is kept for compatibility and appears rarely.

challenge.title: Three moves. No endless exam.
challenge.intro: Choose what each notation means. You get the explanation immediately.
challenge.completeTitle: You can already read a useful chunk of a PGN
challenge.completeBody: Open any analysed game and try to identify these symbols in real moves.

a.label: A bishop captured there and gave check

b.label: A bishop moved there without capturing

q1.explanation: B is bishop, x means capture and + means check.

q2.prompt: What does the longer castling notation mean?
q2.explanation: O-O-O is queenside castling; O-O is kingside castling.

q3.prompt: What is special about this pawn move?

a.label: It promotes to a queen and gives check

b.label: It promotes to a queen and gives checkmate

q3.explanation: =Q is promotion to a queen and # means checkmate.
